results.title: Verified RTL optimization
results.summary: Three contract-preserving RTL transformations across Boolean logic, arithmetic structure, and sequential state representation, each correctness-gated before paired PPA evaluation.
results.problem_statement: Can structurally different RTL transformations reduce implementation-model area, routed delay, or active power while preserving each design's declared functional contract?

evaluation_contract.summary: Each case freezes its interface, correctness semantics, VTR/PTM 45 nm target, primary metrics, and paired acceptance policy before the accepted RTL is compared with its baseline. Correctness failure blocks PPA acceptance.

website.card_summary: Three correctness-gated RTL transformations span Boolean simplification, arithmetic restructuring, and sequential state representation.

figure_captions.assets/evidence-contract.svg: The common evidence boundary: freeze the contract, verify correctness, measure PPA on the pinned target, then apply fixed paired acceptance.
figure_captions.assets/transformation-regimes.svg: Three distinct transformation regimes represented by the public portfolio.
figure_captions.assets/sha1-transform.svg: SHA-1: shared Boolean terms and direct state readout replace duplicated logic and a temporary concatenation.
figure_captions.assets/int8-transform.svg: INT8 MatVec: pairwise 17-bit sums and a balanced 18-bit tree replace repeated 32-bit extension and wide chained accumulation.
figure_captions.assets/mlkem-transform.svg: ML-KEM CBD: a fixed 24-bit physical shift plus a two-bit phase preserves the same logical 1,096-bit state view.

website.score_note: There is no pooled portfolio score. Every percentage is a case-local paired estimate under that circuit's frozen evaluation contract.

results.title: Quadrature rule optimization
results.summary: A compact five-node rule for estimating one-dimensional integrals, improved against a fixed public test suite. The report separates the acceptance score from direct residual errors so the gain can be inspected, replayed, and challenged.
results.problem_statement: Find a compact quadrature rule that reduces integration error across a fixed suite of analytic functions while keeping the rule inspectable, replayable, and stable under the unchanged evaluation contract.

evaluation_contract.summary: Candidates are scored on a frozen analytic integrand suite using a lower-is-better objective. The objective is the acceptance contract, while the report also exposes per-integrand errors as the more interpretable scientific readout.

website.card_summary: A five-node integration rule is compared against a fixed baseline, with both the acceptance score and direct residual errors exposed.

figure_captions.assets/objective-curve.svg: Best-so-far objective over the curated public trace. The acceptance score is lower-is-better and should be read as the contract used to retain candidates.
figure_captions.assets/candidate-trace.svg: Accepted quadrature rule: node positions, normalized weights, and residual error by representative integrand.

website.score_note: The objective is the evaluation contract used by the run, not a universal measure of integration quality. The scientific interpretation comes from reading it together with the residual errors and the replayable candidate.

results.title: PSPLIB J30 scheduling benchmark
results.summary: Across accepted checkpoints under one frozen PSPLIB J30 contract, Evölther reduced the lower-is-better scheduling score from 14.312 at baseline to 12.087, and Evölther 2.0 reduced it further to 10.108 while preserving feasibility on all 80 instances.
results.problem_statement: Find a deterministic activity-priority rule for serial schedule generation that reduces makespan gap against proven PSPLIB J30 optima while preserving precedence and renewable-resource feasibility.

evaluation_contract.summary: Candidates are scored on 80 frozen PSPLIB J30 single-mode RCPSP instances. Every evaluated instance has a proven optimal makespan, and schedules must satisfy precedence constraints, renewable-resource capacities, finite priority scores, and deterministic eligible-activity selection.

website.card_summary: A deterministic scheduling policy reaches a 29.37% lower governed score while preserving feasibility across the frozen portfolio.

figure_captions.assets/objective-curve.svg: Accepted-checkpoint progression from baseline through Evölther and Evölther 2.0 under one unchanged objective.
figure_captions.assets/benchmark-comparison.svg: Baseline, Evölther, and Evölther 2.0 comparison across the frozen portfolio.
figure_captions.assets/resource-load.svg: Actual renewable-resource profiles for baseline and Evölther 2.0 on j3025_9; capacities remain unchanged.
figure_captions.assets/instance-comparison.svg: Task-level baseline-to-Evölther 2.0 schedule comparison for j3025_9, from makespan 112 to 92 against optimum 84.
figure_captions.assets/portfolio-instance-deltas.svg: All 80 instance outcomes against baseline: 35 improved, 27 unchanged, and 18 worse.
figure_captions.assets/gap-readout.svg: Evölther 2.0 aggregate and tail diagnostics on the frozen portfolio.
figure_captions.assets/tail-gap-ladder.svg: Largest remaining Evölther 2.0 gaps against proven optimum.
figure_captions.assets/schedule-network.svg: RCPSP precedence and serial schedule-generation primer.
figure_captions.artifacts/schedule-example.json: Deterministic before-and-after schedule and renewable-resource profiles for j3025_9.

website.score_note: The score is the frozen evaluation contract for this public PSPLIB J30 subset. It is not a runtime benchmark and it is not a claim over all RCPSP instances.

results.title: Exact 26-circle unit-square packing
results.summary: Evölther 2.0 leads the manifested public corpus under three separately verified tolerance contracts and supplies a rational interval proof of strict local optimality for the nearby 78-contact root.
results.problem_statement: Place 26 variable-radius circles inside the unit square and maximize their total radius, keeping the 1e-6, 1e-10, and zero-tolerance feasibility contracts separate.

evaluation_contract.summary: Finite-decimal certificates are parsed as exact rationals and evaluated independently at tolerance 1e-6, 1e-10, and zero. Each check covers 104 walls, 325 pairs, and 26 positive radii.

website.card_summary: Three tolerance-aware corpus leaders plus an exact rational certificate of strict local optimality for one 78-contact configuration.
website.score_note: The governed score is negative exact total radius. The publication leads with sum radii and exact feasibility; the previous floating reconstruction is historical context only.

results.title: Qubit routing LightSABRE benchmark
results.summary: A deterministic qubit-routing policy is replayed against a frozen 24-circuit LightSABRE portfolio across Q20, Willow, and Heron-FEZ topology targets. The accepted candidate reduces aggregate added CNOTs by 12,294 while keeping the topology split and case-level readout public.
results.problem_statement: Find a deterministic routing policy that maps logical two-qubit interactions onto nearest-neighbor hardware coupling graphs while reducing added CNOT count against the fixed LightSABRE reference.

evaluation_contract.summary: Candidates are evaluated on 24 benchmark circuits crossed with Q20, Willow, and Heron-FEZ coupling graphs. The evaluator compares added CNOT count against LightSABRE, uses a lower-is-better negative weighted CNOT-reduction score, and requires deterministic replay validity across all 72 cases.

website.card_summary: A routing policy is replayed against LightSABRE on a frozen 72-case portfolio across Q20, Willow, and Heron-FEZ targets.

figure_captions.assets/objective-curve.svg: Objective trace for the curated public chain. Faint points are scored candidates, the solid line is retained best-so-far weighted CNOT reduction, and rings mark baseline and accepted.
figure_captions.assets/target-comparison.svg: Per-topology added-CNOT comparison for Q20, Willow, and Heron-FEZ. Shorter accepted bars mean fewer added CNOTs than the LightSABRE reference.
figure_captions.assets/routing-readout.svg: Selected largest case-level savings from the replay export, sorted by absolute CNOT reduction versus LightSABRE.

website.score_note: The governed score is the negative weighted CNOT reduction versus LightSABRE, so lower is better. The report also shows positive CNOT reductions because that is the more readable routing-quality readout.

results.title: Iberian BESS Policy Challenge
results.summary: A deterministic BESS dispatch policy is challenged against frozen Iberian day-ahead scenarios, commercial baselines, and a perfect-foresight upper bound with explicit risk and constraint readouts.
results.problem_statement: Improve offline battery dispatch policy quality for OMIE day-ahead price scenarios without violating power, state-of-charge, efficiency, or terminal SOC constraints.

evaluation_contract.summary: Iberian BESS Policy Challenge v0.1: frozen 24-hour OMIE scenarios, commercial baselines, oracle upper bound, degradation proxy, downside metrics, and public-claim guardrails.

website.card_summary: Replayable 1 MW / 4 MWh BESS challenger with 33.714% relative score reduction, €20.20/day mean gross uplift versus the quantile baseline, and 0 constraint breaches across 8 frozen OMIE scenarios.
website.score_note: The score is a weighted euro-like benchmark objective over regret, quantile-baseline shortfall, degradation proxy, downside rate, and constraint penalties. Mean uplift is gross simulated day-ahead dispatch-profit uplift before the degradation proxy; cycle-adjusted margin reports that proxy separately. Intraday and reserve revenues, imbalance settlement, taxes, grid and portfolio effects, and production bidding constraints are excluded.

figure_captions.assets/objective-curve.svg: Seed, checked-in, and accepted policy scores under the v0.1 contract. Lower is better.
figure_captions.assets/baseline-comparison.svg: Accepted policy readout across uplift, regret, cycle-adjusted margin, downside, and constraint breaches.
figure_captions.assets/dispatch-readout.svg: Scenario-level dispatch trace: price, charge/discharge action, and state of charge.
